subject.title: feat: add Podman agent sandbox backend

question: When configured `backend: "docker"` falls back because the Docker CLI is absent, must an explicit backend policy also allow `podman`, or does allowing `docker` intentionally authorize either effective engine?
rationale: `allowBackends` is a security-sensitive operator contract, and code review cannot choose whether it represents configured product identity or the executable engine that actually enforces the sandbox.

options.title: Require effective-engine authorization
options.body: Allow automatic fallback only when unrestricted or when the policy also allowlists `podman`, and surface configured and effective identities separately.

options.title: Authorize by configured identity
options.body: Explicitly approve and test that allowing `docker` also authorizes Podman fallback, with prompts and diagnostics showing both identities.

options.title: Remove automatic fallback
options.body: Keep Docker strictly Docker-only and require users to select and authorize `backend: "podman"` explicitly.

recommendation.title: Require effective-engine authorization
recommendation.body: Allow automatic fallback only when unrestricted or when the policy also allowlists `podman`, and surface configured and effective identities separately.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current shared-engine refactor and are best positioned to coordinate the intended fallback and authorization semantics.
